transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Connor (Redwood); Sofia, Omar, Elena (Lexana)
---
Summary:
Sofia wants a 6-week POC to validate open-model options for multilingual contract clause extraction and risk scoring. Primary constraints: legal-grade accuracy, low hallucination, Spanish/Portuguese/Russian support, and on-prem/VPC options for sensitive files. Redwood to propose 3-model shortlist (+quantized variants), run small hosted benchmark, and provide cost/latency projections and security docs.
Topics covered:
- Workload sizing: tokens per contract, QPS, concurrency, retention policy
- Success criteria: precision/recall targets for clause extraction, acceptable latency, failure modes
- Model shortlist: candidate open models and size tradeoffs
- Benchmarks: dataset, metrics, evaluation cadence
- Timeline & next steps
---
Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sofia (Lexana): hi hi, Sofia here. Head of ML.
[00:09] Omar: Omar, lead counsel. i'll mostly listen but will flag legal constraints.
[00:12] Elena: Elena, PM. focusing on scope and timelines.
[00:15] Connor (Redwood): Connor, infra/SE. i'll run the bench and the hosting setup.
[00:20] Maya: Cool. high level — Lexana wants to run a POC to compare model options for clause extraction and risk scoring across english, spanish, portuguese, and russian. Is that right, Sofia?
[00:29] Sofia: Yes, exact. we also want to measure hallucination rates when models are asked to synthesize missing clauses, and false positives on liability clauses.
[00:35] Omar: also data residency — some contracts from EU clients require data remain in our VPC or an on-prem instance. SOC 2 is baseline, but some customers ask for ISO or audit logs and HSM/KMS.
[00:45] Maya: that's helpful. we can do Hosted for initial runs but will propose Dedicated / Private for production. Redwood has audit logs and KMS integrations; we'll send the security brief. sorry — our security deck.
[00:53] Elena: timeline constraint: we want results before the legal review cycle in mid July, so roughly a six-week window.
[01:00] Connor: noted. to scope infra: can you give rough workload numbers — average contract length, number of docs per day, peak concurrent reviewers?
[01:08] Sofia: average contract is ~3,500 tokens, some long ones up to 12k. we'll pilot with 200 anonymized contracts (mix of standard NDAs, SOWs, supplier contracts). Daily throughput target for POC ~500 documents, peak concurrent users maybe 40.
[01:20] Connor: ok that maps to qps and token throughput. for early bench we can simulate 50 QPS with batching. production expectations?
[01:27] Sofia: production could be 2k docs/day, but POC should demonstrate we can meet ~500/day with sub-second-ish latency per clause extraction call.
[01:35] Maya: let's talk success criteria — what metrics will you use to decide go/no-go?
[01:40] Elena: primary: clause extraction F1 >= 0.85 for key clause types (termination, indemnity, liability). secondary: hallucination rate < 2% on generative answers, latency < 800 ms for single-document extract endpoint, and cost per document under $0.05 for hosted.
[01:55] Sofia: and multilingual performance: for Spanish/Portuguese we want within 5 percentage points of English performance; russian is lower priority but should not be catastrophic.
[02:05] Omar: compliance: all PII must be redacted and logs should be configurable to avoid storing full text in Redwood logs.
[02:12] Connor: we support redaction and KV/prefix cache controls; will note retention config and masking.
[02:17] Maya: model shortlist — based on your domain we recommend testing a small, medium, and a larger open model variant. initial candidates: 1) LlamaX-13B (quantized 4-bit), 2) Orion-33B (unoptimized), 3) JurisGPT-70B-open (if available) — plus distilled / quantized variants. any concerns?
[02:36] Sofia: JurisGPT — is that an external community model? i've heard inconsistent results.
[02:40] Maya: yes community-sourced, tends to be best-in-class for legal prompts but can be less stable on hallucinations. that's why we'll include a medium-sized generalist model as a control.
[02:49] Connor: tradeoffs — 13B quantized will be cheapest and fast with decent accuracy; 33B is a middle ground; 70B likely best accuracy but higher cost and may need Dedicated or higher GPU to meet latency. we can also test smart rerouting: run extractors on 13B and fallback to 70B for low-confidence cases.
[03:05] Elena: fallback policy sounds promising. can we measure reroute latency?
[03:08] Connor: yes we'll instrument trace — expected extra latency if fallback is invoked, but only for small percent of requests.
[03:14] Sofia: what's Redwood's approach to model quantization? are we losing crucial legal nuance?
[03:18] Connor: quantization degrades some subtlety but with instruction-tuning and careful prompt engineering it's often acceptable for extraction tasks. for scoring/risk we might need the larger model. we'll include a quality delta table in the bench.
[03:29] [crosstalk] Omar: and what about fine-tuning vs prompt engineering?
[03:32] Maya: for POC we recommend prompt & eval-first to avoid long fine-tune cycles. If results plateau, we can do a small instruction-tune or RLHF later — which would change timeline.
[03:41] Elena: budget? we have limited budget for this quarter. can you give rough cost brackets?
[03:45] Maya: ballpark for 2-week hosted bench: small model runs maybe $800-$1.2k, mid model $2k-$3k, large $6k+. Production cost depends on tokens and model—we'll provide per-doc estimates.
[03:58] Sofia: ok that's fine as a preliminary.
[04:00] Connor: benchmark plan:
- Week 0: ingest and sanitize 200 contracts (Sofia)
- Week 1: run smoke tests on 13B quantized and 33B baseline (hosted) for extraction metrics
- Week 2: run larger 70B test and fallback policy sim
- Week 3: stress tests for throughput (simulate 500/day, peak 40 concurrent)
- Week 4: compile results, meeting to review and recommend production config
[04:25] Elena: that fits the 6-week window if we start asap.
[04:28] Maya: security items — we'll send SOC 2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, SAML SSO, and KMS docs. any extra certs?
[04:36] Omar: for certain clients we may need on-prem or private deployment and HSM integration. also legal wants to see data deletion audit trail.
[04:44] Connor: Private deployment is supported; scheduling and hardware planning would add ~4–6 weeks after POC if you choose that route.
[04:52] Sofia: can Redwood provide a sample evaluation script so we can reproduce metrics?
[04:55] Connor: yes we'll share our benchmark harness and a reproducible notebook (will include tokenization, metrics, and conf intervals).
[05:01] Maya: any competitors or internal constraints we should be aware of?
[05:04] Sofia: we did preliminary tests with Bedrock and OpenAI; Bedrock was cheaper but we had trouble with fine-grained extraction, OpenAI had best out-of-the-box but cost is a worry.
[05:15] Omar: legal also flagged vendor lock-in risk.
[05:18] Maya: that's a good point — Redwood's exportable prompts and pinned model versions help reduce lock-in. we'll document the model artifacts and configs.
[05:25] Elena: final recap and next steps?
[05:27] Maya: recap: Lexana provides 200 anonymized contracts + label set by 2026-05-18. Redwood shares benchmark spreadsheet, security brief, and sample notebook by 2026-05-16. Connor to provision hosted trial and run initial 13B/33B smoke by 2026-05-20. We'll target a POC kickoff run week of 2026-05-25.
[05:45] Sofia: sounds good. Omar — any final?
[05:48] Omar: just please include deletion audit detail in the security brief.
[05:52] Maya: will do. thanks all.
[05:55] End of call.
